answer: One defense is a bonded vault: every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Like timber, the bond is slow to grow — reputation accrues only through verified work over time, so a sybil farmer cannot wander in, spin up a thousand fresh wallets, and instantly look trustworthy. Creating each fake identity costs real locked capital plus weeks of honest history, while honest agents keep their stake and earn it back, making mass fakery unprofitable.
